solution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer table gives \(\cot 315^\circ = 1\), contradicting its own \(\tan 315^\circ = -1\) in the same column. Since \(315^\circ\) lies in the fourth quadrant, \(\cot 315^\circ = -1\), as given below. All other cells of both printed tables agree with this answer.]

Reduce each angle to its related acute angle and attach the sign of its quadrant (a negative angle is coterminal with the angle got by adding \(360^\circ\)): quadrant I \(-300^\circ\equiv 60^\circ\), \(-330^\circ\equiv 30^\circ\); quadrant II \(120^\circ\), \(-210^\circ\equiv 150^\circ\); quadrant III \(225^\circ\), \(240^\circ\), \(-120^\circ\equiv 240^\circ\), \(-150^\circ\equiv 210^\circ\); quadrant IV \(315^\circ\); and \(90^\circ\), \(270^\circ\), \(-180^\circ\) are quadrantal. (N.D. = not defined.)

| Angle | \(\sin\) | \(\cos\) | \(\tan\) | \(\operatorname{cosec}\) | \(\sec\) | \(\cot\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(90^\circ\) | \(1\) | \(0\) | N.D. | \(1\) | N.D. | \(0\) |
| \(120^\circ\) | \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(-\frac{1}{2}\) | \(-\sqrt{3}\) | \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(-2\) | \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) |
| \(225^\circ\) | \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) | \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) | \(1\) | \(-\sqrt{2}\) | \(-\sqrt{2}\) | \(1\) |
| \(240^\circ\) | \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(-\frac{1}{2}\) | \(\sqrt{3}\) | \(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(-2\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) |
| \(270^\circ\) | \(-1\) | \(0\) | N.D. | \(-1\) | N.D. | \(0\) |
| \(315^\circ\) | \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) | \(-1\) | \(-\sqrt{2}\) | \(\sqrt{2}\) | \(-1\) |
| \(-120^\circ\) | \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(-\frac{1}{2}\) | \(\sqrt{3}\) | \(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(-2\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) |
| \(-150^\circ\) | \(-\frac{1}{2}\) | \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(-2\) | \(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(\sqrt{3}\) |
| \(-180^\circ\) | \(0\) | \(-1\) | \(0\) | N.D. | \(-1\) | N.D. |
| \(-210^\circ\) | \(\frac{1}{2}\) | \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(2\) | \(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(-\sqrt{3}\) |
| \(-300^\circ\) | \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(\frac{1}{2}\) | \(\sqrt{3}\) | \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(2\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) |
| \(-330^\circ\) | \(\frac{1}{2}\) | \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) | \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(2\) | \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) | \(\sqrt{3}\) |
_note: The book's answer table prints \(\cot 315^\circ = 1\). That contradicts its own entry \(\tan 315^\circ = -1\) in the same column, since \(\cot\theta = 1/\tan\theta\). \(315^\circ\) lies in quadrant IV, where \(\cot\) is negative, so \(\cot 315^\circ = -1\). Every other cell of both book tables was checked and agrees with the values given here.

solution: \(520^\circ = 360^\circ + 160^\circ\), so \(520^\circ\) is coterminal with \(160^\circ\), which lies in quadrant II. In quadrant II \(\sin\) is positive, hence so is \(\operatorname{cosec}\). \(\operatorname{cosec} 520^\circ\) is positive.

\(1899^\circ = 5\times 360^\circ + 99^\circ = 1800^\circ + 99^\circ\), so \(1899^\circ\) is coterminal with \(99^\circ\), which lies in quadrant II. In quadrant II only \(\sin\) and \(\operatorname{cosec}\) are positive, so \(\cot\) is negative. \(\cot 1899^\circ\) is negative.

\(986^\circ = 2\times 360^\circ + 266^\circ = 720^\circ + 266^\circ\), so \(986^\circ\) is coterminal with \(266^\circ\), which lies in quadrant III. In quadrant III \(\sin\) is negative. \(\sin 986^\circ\) is negative.

\(\sec\theta > 0\) means \(\cos\theta > 0\), so \(\theta\) lies in quadrant I or IV. \(\tan\theta < 0\) holds in quadrants II and IV. The quadrant common to both conditions is IV. \(\theta\) lies in quadrant IV.
\(\sin\theta < 0\) holds in quadrants III and IV; \(\cos\theta < 0\) holds in quadrants II and III. The quadrant common to both conditions is III. \(\theta\) lies in quadrant III.
\(\sin\theta > 0\) holds in quadrants I and II; \(\tan\theta < 0\) holds in quadrants II and IV. The quadrant common to both conditions is II. \(\theta\) lies in quadrant II.

Subtract multiples of \(360^\circ\). \(1856^\circ = 5\times 360^\circ + 56^\circ\), so \(\sin 1856^\circ = \sin 56^\circ\), and \(56^\circ\) is in quadrant I, so \(\sin 1856^\circ > 0\).
\(2006^\circ = 5\times 360^\circ + 206^\circ\), so \(\sin 2006^\circ = \sin 206^\circ = \sin(180^\circ + 26^\circ) = -\sin 26^\circ < 0\).
A positive number is greater than a negative one, so \(\sin 1856^\circ > \sin 2006^\circ\).

\(310^\circ\) lies in quadrant IV, where \(\sin\) is negative, so \(\sin 310^\circ < 0\). Since \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\), \(\sin(-310^\circ) = -\sin 310^\circ > 0\); equivalently \(-310^\circ\) is coterminal with \(-310^\circ + 360^\circ = 50^\circ\), which lies in quadrant I. Hence \(\sin(-310^\circ)\) is positive.

Replace \(1\) by \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta\):
\(1 - 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta - 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = (\sin\theta - \cos\theta)^2\).
For every real \(\theta\), \(\sin\theta - \cos\theta\) is a real number and the square of a real number is never negative. Hence \(1 - 2\sin\theta\cos\theta \ge 0\) for all \(\theta \in \mathbb{R}\).

[Textbook misprint: the question states "for all \(\theta \in R\)", but \(\tan\theta\) and \(\cot\theta\) are undefined at integer multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). The inequality is proved below on the common domain, i.e. for every \(\theta\) that is not an integer multiple of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).]

Since \(\tan\theta \cdot \cot\theta = 1\), we may write \(2 = 2\tan\theta\cot\theta\). Then
\(\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta - 2 = \tan^2\theta - 2\tan\theta\cot\theta + \cot^2\theta = (\tan\theta - \cot\theta)^2 \ge 0\),
since it is the square of a real number. Transposing, \(\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta \ge 2\) for every \(\theta\) at which \(\tan\theta\) and \(\cot\theta\) are defined, i.e. for all \(\theta \ne \frac{n\pi}{2}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
_note: The stem says "for all \(\theta \in R\)", but \(\tan\theta\) is undefined at \(\theta = (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\cot\theta\) is undefined at \(\theta = n\pi\), so the expression does not exist at \(\theta = \frac{n\pi}{2}\). The intended claim, proved here, is for all \(\theta\) other than integer multiples of \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).

solution:
\(\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta = 1 - \frac{(x^2-y^2)^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2} = \frac{(x^2+y^2)^2 - (x^2-y^2)^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\).
By \(a^2 - b^2 = (a+b)(a-b)\) with \(a = x^2+y^2\) and \(b = x^2-y^2\), the numerator is \((2x^2)(2y^2) = 4x^2y^2\), so \(\cos^2\theta = \frac{4x^2y^2}{(x^2+y^2)^2}\) and \(\cos\theta = \pm\frac{2xy}{x^2+y^2}\). Taking the positive value,
\(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{x^2-y^2}{x^2+y^2} \times \frac{x^2+y^2}{2xy} = \frac{x^2-y^2}{2xy}\).
Hence \(\cos\theta = \frac{2xy}{x^2+y^2}\) and \(\tan\theta = \frac{x^2-y^2}{2xy}\).

\(\frac{3\pi}{2} < \theta < 2\pi\) places \(\theta\) in quadrant IV, where \(\cos\theta > 0\) and \(\sin\theta < 0\).
From \(\sec\theta = \sqrt{2}\) we get \(\cos\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\sin\theta = -\sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{2}} = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\).
Hence \(\tan\theta = -1\), \(\cot\theta = -1\), \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta = -\sqrt{2}\).
\(\frac{1+\tan\theta+\operatorname{cosec}\theta}{1+\cot\theta-\operatorname{cosec}\theta} = \frac{1 - 1 - \sqrt{2}}{1 - 1 + \sqrt{2}} = \frac{-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = -1\).
The value of the expression is \(-1\).

Group the terms containing \(\cos^2 B\) and those containing \(\sin^2 B\):
L.H.S. \(= \cos^2 B(\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) + \sin^2 B(\cos^2 A + \sin^2 A)\)
\(= \cos^2 B \times 1 + \sin^2 B \times 1 = \sin^2 B + \cos^2 B = 1 = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\sin^2 A\cos^2 B + \cos^2 A\sin^2 B + \cos^2 A\cos^2 B + \sin^2 A\sin^2 B = 1\).

First factor of the numerator:
\(1 + \cot\theta + \tan\theta = 1 + \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} + \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{\sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{1+\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\).
Denominator:
\(\sec^3\theta - \operatorname{cosec}^3\theta = \frac{1}{\cos^3\theta} - \frac{1}{\sin^3\theta} = \frac{\sin^3\theta - \cos^3\theta}{\sin^3\theta\cos^3\theta}\),
and \(\sin^3\theta - \cos^3\theta = (\sin\theta-\cos\theta)(\sin^2\theta + \sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta) = (\sin\theta-\cos\theta)(1+\sin\theta\cos\theta)\).
Therefore
L.H.S. \(= \frac{(1+\sin\theta\cos\theta)(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} \times \frac{\sin^3\theta\cos^3\theta}{(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)(1+\sin\theta\cos\theta)} = \frac{\sin^3\theta\cos^3\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\frac{(1+\cot\theta+\tan\theta)(\sin\theta-\cos\theta)}{\sec^3\theta-\operatorname{cosec}^3\theta} = \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\).

Use \((a+b)^2 + (a-b)^2 = 2a^2 + 2b^2\) with \(a = \tan\theta\) and \(b = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} = \sec\theta\):
L.H.S. \(= 2\tan^2\theta + 2\sec^2\theta = 2\left(\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} + \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta}\right) = \frac{2(1+\sin^2\theta)}{\cos^2\theta}\).
Since \(\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta\), this equals \(2\left(\frac{1+\sin^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}\right) = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\left(\tan\theta+\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\right)^2 + \left(\tan\theta-\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{1+\sin^2\theta}{1-\sin^2\theta}\right)\).

Take the two \(\sec\) terms together and use \(\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta\):
\(2\sec^2\theta - \sec^4\theta = \sec^2\theta(2 - \sec^2\theta) = (1+\tan^2\theta)(2 - 1 - \tan^2\theta) = (1+\tan^2\theta)(1-\tan^2\theta) = 1 - \tan^4\theta\).
In exactly the same way, with \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta = 1 + \cot^2\theta\),
\(2\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \operatorname{cosec}^4\theta = 1 - \cot^4\theta\), so \(-2\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta + \operatorname{cosec}^4\theta = \cot^4\theta - 1\).
Adding, L.H.S. \(= (1 - \tan^4\theta) + (\cot^4\theta - 1) = \cot^4\theta - \tan^4\theta = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(2\sec^2\theta - \sec^4\theta - 2\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta + \operatorname{cosec}^4\theta = \cot^4\theta - \tan^4\theta\).

Use \(a^2 + b^2 = (a+b)^2 - 2ab\) with \(a = \sin^2\theta\) and \(b = \cos^2\theta\):
L.H.S. \(= (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)^2 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1^2 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\).

Write \(p = \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\). With \(a = \sin^2\theta\), \(b = \cos^2\theta\) we have \(a + b = 1\), so
\(\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta = (a+b)^3 - 3ab(a+b) = 1 - 3p\) and \(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta = (a+b)^2 - 2ab = 1 - 2p\).
Substituting,
L.H.S. \(= 2(1-3p) - 3(1-2p) + 1 = 2 - 6p - 3 + 6p + 1 = 0 = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(2(\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta) - 3(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta) + 1 = 0\).

Factorise the difference of squares:
L.H.S. \(= (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta) + 1 = (\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)\times 1 + 1\).
Now put \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta\):
\(= \cos^2\theta - (1 - \cos^2\theta) + 1 = 2\cos^2\theta = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\cos^4\theta - \sin^4\theta + 1 = 2\cos^2\theta\).

Take \(\sin^2\theta\) common and use \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\):
L.H.S. \(= \sin^2\theta(\sin^2\theta + 2\cos^2\theta) = \sin^2\theta\big[(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) + \cos^2\theta\big] = \sin^2\theta(1 + \cos^2\theta)\).
Replacing \(\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta\),
\(= (1 - \cos^2\theta)(1 + \cos^2\theta) = 1 - \cos^4\theta = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\sin^4\theta + 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1 - \cos^4\theta\).

Use \(a^3 + b^3 = (a+b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)\) and \(a^3 - b^3 = (a-b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)\) with \(a = \sin\theta\), \(b = \cos\theta\), and cancel:
\(\frac{\sin^3\theta + \cos^3\theta}{\sin\theta + \cos\theta} = \sin^2\theta - \sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin\theta\cos\theta\),
\(\frac{\sin^3\theta - \cos^3\theta}{\sin\theta - \cos\theta} = \sin^2\theta + \sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1 + \sin\theta\cos\theta\).
Adding, L.H.S. \(= (1 - \sin\theta\cos\theta) + (1 + \sin\theta\cos\theta) = 2 = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\frac{\sin^3\theta + \cos^3\theta}{\sin\theta + \cos\theta} + \frac{\sin^3\theta - \cos^3\theta}{\sin\theta - \cos\theta} = 2\).

Write \(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) and take \(\sin^2\theta\) common:
L.H.S. \(= \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} - \sin^2\theta = \sin^2\theta\left(\frac{1 - \cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}\right) = \sin^2\theta \times \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = \sin^4\theta\sec^2\theta = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\tan^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \sin^4\theta\sec^2\theta\).

Expand both squares, using \(\sin\theta\cdot\operatorname{cosec}\theta = 1\) and \(\cos\theta\cdot\sec\theta = 1\):
L.H.S. \(= (\sin^2\theta + 2 + \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta) + (\cos^2\theta + 2 + \sec^2\theta)\)
\(= (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) + 4 + \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta + \sec^2\theta = 5 + \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta + \sec^2\theta\).
Now \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta = 1 + \cot^2\theta\) and \(\sec^2\theta = 1 + \tan^2\theta\), so
\(= 5 + (1+\cot^2\theta) + (1+\tan^2\theta) = \tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta + 7 = \) R.H.S.
Hence \((\sin\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta)^2 + (\cos\theta + \sec\theta)^2 = \tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta + 7\).

Treat the left side as a difference of squares twice:
L.H.S. \(= (\sin^4\theta)^2 - (\cos^4\theta)^2 = (\sin^4\theta - \cos^4\theta)(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta)\).
Now \(\sin^4\theta - \cos^4\theta = (\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta)(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) = \sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta\),
and \(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta = (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)^2 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\).
Multiplying, L.H.S. \(= (\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta)(1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta) = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\sin^8\theta - \cos^8\theta = (\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta)(1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta)\).

With \(a = \sin^2 A\), \(b = \cos^2 A\) we have \(a + b = 1\), so by \(a^3 + b^3 = (a+b)^3 - 3ab(a+b)\),
L.H.S. \(= 1 - 3\sin^2 A\cos^2 A\).
Replace \(\cos^2 A = 1 - \sin^2 A\):
\(= 1 - 3\sin^2 A(1 - \sin^2 A) = 1 - 3\sin^2 A + 3\sin^4 A = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\sin^6 A + \cos^6 A = 1 - 3\sin^2 A + 3\sin^4 A\).

Expand both squares; the middle terms \(\pm 2\tan A\tan B\) cancel:
L.H.S. \(= (1 + 2\tan A\tan B + \tan^2 A\tan^2 B) + (\tan^2 A - 2\tan A\tan B + \tan^2 B)\)
\(= 1 + \tan^2 A + \tan^2 B + \tan^2 A\tan^2 B\).
Group and factorise:
\(= (1 + \tan^2 A) + \tan^2 B(1 + \tan^2 A) = (1+\tan^2 A)(1+\tan^2 B) = \sec^2 A\cdot\sec^2 B = \) R.H.S.
Hence \((1 + \tan A\tan B)^2 + (\tan A - \tan B)^2 = \sec^2 A\cdot\sec^2 B\).

Use \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1\), i.e. \(1 = (\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta - \cot\theta)\), on the constant term of each numerator.
L.H.S. numerator \(= (\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-\cot\theta) + \cot\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta = (\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta - \cot\theta + 1)\), and its denominator is \(1 - \cot\theta + \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \operatorname{cosec}\theta - \cot\theta + 1\). Cancelling,
L.H.S. \(= \operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta\).
R.H.S. numerator \(= (\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta) - (\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-\cot\theta) = (\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta)(1 - \operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta)\), and its denominator is \(\cot\theta - \operatorname{cosec}\theta + 1 = 1 + \cot\theta - \operatorname{cosec}\theta\). Cancelling,
R.H.S. \(= \operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta\).
Both sides reduce to \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta\), hence \(\frac{1+\cot\theta+\operatorname{cosec}\theta}{1-\cot\theta+\operatorname{cosec}\theta} = \frac{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta-1}{\cot\theta-\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1}\).

From \(\sec^2\theta - 1 = \tan^2\theta\) we get \((\sec\theta-1)(\sec\theta+1) = \tan^2\theta\), so \(\sec\theta - 1 = \frac{\tan^2\theta}{\sec\theta+1}\).
Hence the numerator of the L.H.S. is
\(\tan\theta + (\sec\theta - 1) = \tan\theta + \frac{\tan^2\theta}{\sec\theta+1} = \frac{\tan\theta(\sec\theta + 1 + \tan\theta)}{\sec\theta+1}\).
Therefore
L.H.S. \(= \frac{\tan\theta(\tan\theta+\sec\theta+1)}{(\sec\theta+1)(\tan\theta+\sec\theta+1)} = \frac{\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+1} = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\frac{\tan\theta+\sec\theta-1}{\tan\theta+\sec\theta+1} = \frac{\tan\theta}{\sec\theta+1}\).

From \(\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - 1 = \cot^2\theta\) we get \((\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1) = \cot^2\theta\), so \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta - 1 = \frac{\cot^2\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1}\).
Hence the numerator of the L.H.S. is
\(\cot\theta + (\operatorname{cosec}\theta - 1) = \cot\theta + \frac{\cot^2\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1} = \frac{\cot\theta(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + 1 + \cot\theta)}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1}\),
so L.H.S. \(= \frac{\cot\theta(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta+1)}{(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta+1)} = \frac{\cot\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1} = \frac{\cos\theta/\sin\theta}{(1+\sin\theta)/\sin\theta} = \frac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}\).
Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(1-\sin\theta\),
\(= \frac{\cos\theta(1-\sin\theta)}{1-\sin^2\theta} = \frac{\cos\theta(1-\sin\theta)}{\cos^2\theta} = \frac{1-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\frac{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta-1}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta+1} = \frac{1-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\).

From \(\cot^2\theta = \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - 1 = (\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta+1)\) we get \(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + 1 = \frac{\cot^2\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1}\).
Hence the numerator of the L.H.S. is
\(\cot\theta + (\operatorname{cosec}\theta + 1) = \cot\theta + \frac{\cot^2\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1} = \frac{\cot\theta(\operatorname{cosec}\theta - 1 + \cot\theta)}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1}\).
Therefore
L.H.S. \(= \frac{\cot\theta(\cot\theta+\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1)}{(\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1)(\cot\theta+\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1)} = \frac{\cot\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1} = \) R.H.S.
Hence \(\frac{\operatorname{cosec}\theta+\cot\theta+1}{\cot\theta+\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1} = \frac{\cot\theta}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta-1}\).
